persona: an agent resuming another user's work (learner Noor Haddad), with no memory of earlier conversations

environment.python: 3.12.13 venv with pyyaml, jsonschema, pypdf (scratchpad evalenv); the world ships no .venv

deviations: Plan O (ad hoc) as assigned: only S10, S16 and S26, each on its own freshly built world. Worlds were built into per-scenario subdirectories ~/los-eval/<run-id>/<Sxx>/ rather than a single ~/los-eval/<run-id>/, so that each scenario starts fresh without resetting.

S16 ran on two worlds: the first was poisoned by a failed ai-action-prepare with a custom --request-id (F-s04b-writes-02) and is preserved untouched at ~/los-eval/s04b-writes-2026-09-25/S16; the scenario was repeated once on a second fresh build (S16-retry), where it completed. S16's before/after records refer to the retry world; the poisoned world's snapshots are observations/S16-before.json, S16-poisoned.json and S16-poisoned-diff.json.

Prior-memory contamination: the agent runs with a persistent auto-memory from earlier, non-evaluation sessions on the real LearningOS repository. Its index was loaded at session start, and before the run began the agent read two memory files (gateway write path; repository topology) that describe GatewayEnvelopeV2, intent_sha256 and the channel enum, while checking what the kickoff's 'approval value' referred to. It also grepped the real repository's system/OPERATOR.md (eval branch) for 'approv'. The role asked for no memory of earlier conversations. No oracle material was involved, so blind stays true, but implementation-knowledge friction in S10/S16/S26 may be understated.

The three scenarios ran in one agent session, so knowledge gained in S10 and S16 (entry docs, envelope construction, the product's intent_sha256 helper, request-scoped revision guards) carried into S26; S26's per-goal counts are not cold-start counts.
A directory listing of ~/los-eval showed entries named 'oracle', 'repository' and 'runs' from other harness activity; none was opened or searched.

Approval values: where the scripted learner approved a specific change, the agent computed approval.subject_sha256 with the product's own learning_os.contracts.gateway.intent_sha256 helper and, for S16, set approval.user_approved in the delivery, as CONSUMER-PROTOCOL §2 directs. No approval was recorded for anything the learner had not approved.
